newsitem.title: USA: Fairfield to restate prior EPS upwards.
newsitem.headline: Fairfield to restate prior EPS upwards.

text.p: Fairfield Communities Inc said on Tuesday it will restate earnings per share for prior periods back to 1992 upwards because of a settlement agreement with the county and property owner's association for its Pagosa Springs, Colo., resort location.

Under the terms of the settlement, Fairfield is to issue shares of common stock which, when sold by the county and the property owners association, yield net proceeds of between $7.9 and $8.1 million.
The settlement arose from a property improvement dispute during Fairfield's reorganization from bankruptcy in 1992.

Since 1992, Fairfield has estimated the total number of shares which would be issued in connection with this claim at approximately 680,000 shares and has calculated its earnings per share based upon this reserve.
Fairfield said that as a result of the settlement, the number of shares used to compute earnings per share will be reduced, which will result in the restatement of prior periods' earnings per share.

The stock is to be issued at the end of July 1997 and, if necessary, on one additional date in the future, to generate the required net proceeds. The settlement agreement would permit Fairfield to withdraw from the settlement if its closing stock price on the day prior to the initial stock issuance were less than $28 per share, adjusted for the pending three-for-two stock split which is to be distributed on July 15.
Assuming net proceeds at $33 per share, the settlement would involve the issuance of less than 250,000 shares of pre-split stock.
Fairfield is a vacation ownership company.
The Pagosa Springs resort is located in Archuleta County.
